## Per site

- Peten, Guatemala: labels ambiguous 43, loss 84, stable 17; MCC baseline -0.03, best lab:seasonal_loss_either@1 0.18.
- Ketapang, West Kalimantan: labels ambiguous 48, loss 38, not_forest 3, stable 55; MCC baseline 0.49, best registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1 0.49.

- Chaco, Argentina: labels ambiguous 58, loss 17, not_forest 1, stable 68; MCC baseline 0.07, best lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen 0.17.

## Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

| `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` | 0.054 | 0.037 | -0.094 to +0.062 | no clear effect |
| `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` | -0.092 | -0.111 | -0.090 to +0.050 | no clear effect |
| `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` | 0.204 | 0.217 | -0.056 to +0.083 | no clear effect |
| `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` | 0.145 | 0.254 | +0.039 to +0.184 | helps |

## The search, scored on sites it never saw

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.458**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of +0.233 to +0.392: the searched rule beats the registry baseline.
